newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to resume diplomatic activity in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Spain to resume diplomatic activity in Iraq.

text.p: Spain will send a permanent diplomatic representative to its embassy in Iraq within weeks after a nearly six-year hiatus, Foreign Ministry officials said on Monday.
The representative, who has not yet been named, will be a charge d'affaires. Spain hopes to improve relations with Iraq with a view to sending an ambassador in the future, the officials said.
"A diplomat will be sent to resume activities in the embassy in the coming weeks," said a ministry official.

Spain has not had a permanent diplomatic representative at the Baghdad embassy since the 1991 Gulf War. The embassy has operated on an administrative level only and the two countries have maintained diplomatic relations.

The renewal of diplomatic activity at the Spanish embassy is connected to Iraq's resumption of oil sales two weeks ago under an "oil-for-food" deal signed with the United Nations, a second ministry official said.
"It's a moment Spain wants to be present for," said the official, who asked not to be named.
Since Iraq resumed limited oil sales to international markets, several Western countries have indicated they want to re-establish a diplomatic presence in Baghdad.

Baghdad is allowed to sell $2.0 billion worth of oil every six months to raise money for food and medicine, an effort to alleviate suffering from stringent U.N. trade sanctions imposed for a 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Scores of Spanish businessmen and traders have flocked to Baghdad recently to secure deals in the lucrative market. Spain was one of Iraq's major trading partners before the Gulf crisis.
